transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?
I'm coming in today because I've been experiencing hallucinations. I keep hearing voices and seeing things that aren't actually there, and it's really starting to overwhelm me.
How long have you been experiencing these hallucinations, and did they start around the same time as any changes in your mood, such as feeling extremely happy, sad, or irritable?

I've been experiencing the hallucinations for about seven months, and they mostly started when I was feeling incredibly energetic, happy, and easily irritated. That intense mood also lasted for about seven months, but there was a period of at least two weeks where my mood was completely normal while the hallucinations kept happening.

During the time when your mood returned to normal but the hallucinations continued, were you still able to function relatively normally in your daily life, or were the hallucinations significantly interfering with your social and occupational functioning?

I'm not entirely sure how to measure the impact it had on my life during those weeks. The voices and visions were definitely distracting and unsettling, but I can't clearly recall how much they actually interfered with my daily tasks or work.
Have you been experiencing any persistent beliefs or thoughts that seem real to you but are not based in reality, such as thinking you have special powers or that someone is plotting against you?

Yes, I actually have experienced both of those things. I've had times where I felt very strongly that I possess special abilities and powers that others don't, but at the same time, I often feel like people are watching me and plotting against me.
Can you estimate how much of the total time you've been experiencing hallucinations and delusions was spent in a manic or hypomanic state, versus a normal or depressed mood state?

Out of the year and ten months since all of this started, I've spent about seven months in that high-energy, manic state. The depressed periods only lasted for about four months. There were also at least a couple of weeks where I was having the hallucinations and delusions but my mood felt completely normal.

Did the periods of normal mood where hallucinations and delusions occurred last for more than two months at any point, or were they always relatively brief, occurring in between your manic and depressive episodes?

No, those periods never lasted for as long as two months. They were always pretty brief, usually only lasting about two or three weeks. My mood would feel completely normal during those gaps, but the hallucinations and delusions were still happening.
Would you say that the hallucinations and delusions have been the dominant symptoms throughout your illness, or have the manic and depressive episodes been more prominent and disruptive to your life?

Even though the hallucinations and delusions are terrifying, the manic and depressive episodes have felt much more prominent. Those intense mood swings have occupied the majority of the time I've been unwell overall. They've definitely had a bigger impact on my life.

Can you describe a typical episode of mania or depression for you, including how the hallucinations and delusions present during those times, and whether they seem to be triggered by or independent of your mood swings?

During my high periods, I have overflowing energy, talk incredibly fast, and spend money recklessly, whereas my low periods leave me with no motivation, cloudy thinking, and no interest in anything. The hallucinations and delusions definitely happen during these extreme mood episodes, but they also

Do the hallucinations and delusions seem to be directly triggered by the extreme mood episodes, or do they occur independently of your mood swings, and are there any specific events or situations that tend to trigger or worsen the hallucinations and delusions?

While they often happen during my high-energy phases, they definitely occur on their own when my mood is completely normal, sometimes lasting for two weeks or more without any mood swings. I haven't noticed any specific events or situations that trigger them; they just seem to happen independently.
I'm sorry, I think I missed what you were saying. Could you please repeat or clarify your last question for me?
